pos.text: Phenomenal game, unfortunately I now have the perfect amount of played hours and all the achievements so I can never play it again, hopefully a bomb ass sequel will occur and I can once again enjoy this game.

It's one of those games that hooks you before you even realize it. You don’t actually control the hero, you build the world around them. Every card you place changes the loop, spawns new monsters, or gives bonuses, and somehow it all just clicks. The retro art and eerie soundtrack are perfect for the game’s strange, post-apocalyptic vibe. It’s super satisfying to discover new tile combos, but after a while, runs can start feeling a bit samey. Still, for something so simple on the surface, it’s surprisingly deep and addictive.
Fun game! I felt like this could have been so much more with expansions and updates but a good time anyway!

Loop hero has you go on expeditions to try to recover the world from the void that engulfed it. It features some of the most unique pixel art I've seen, really leaning into a 90's dark fantasy style. As you go on expeditions, you collect resources to grow your home camp. While on an expedition, your character fights monsters automatically. The only actions you take as the player are placing terrain cards you get from enemies, equipping newly acquired gear and returning to camp when the time is right.

For me, Loop Hero was a very hand-off experience. Yet it was curiously engaging, with me wanting to progress the story, expand my camp and discover more of what the game had to offer. After about 40 hours and collecting all achievements, I do have some things to say.

Very interesting almost idle RPG game.
Loop Hero is essentially a game where you build the world your character fights through. You don't have much control over your character, instead the game is mostly balancing what you place in their way. 
Too many obstacles or enemies and they could die before they get far. Too little and your character will be woefully unprepared for the chapter boss.
It's quite fun.

Took me a couple runs to actually get what was happening, but once it clicked I lost an entire weekend to this game. The idea of building the world around your hero instead of controlling him directly sounds gimmicky on paper but it works really well in practice. Every card placement is a small decision that compounds over time, and you're constantly asking yourself whether you're making the loop harder than you can handle 

.The meta progression never feels like a grind, and the atmosphere is oddly cozy for a game about an apocalypse. The lo-fi soundtrack helps a lot with that. Only complaint is that once you've figured out a few strong builds it can get a bit samey. But getting there takes a while and the journey is worth it.
solid ~30-40 hour timesink. You’re tuning enemy density, scaling, and build synergies yourself, balancing pressure and payoff, then deciding how far to push before pulling out alive.
interesting and fresh concept but the more you play it, the more tedious it feels

pure soul, best art and music direction in the past 10 years

please make a sequel!

At the same time, the game still has the weakness of feeling like "this is all just simply one big materials grind, I'm just repeating the same thing to get my numbers to go up."  I kind of wish that you weren't penalized every time you try to seriously do a run where you attempt to clear a boss, it encourages the player to just grind the maps over and over, as opposed to more classic roguelikes like Shiren the Wanderer where you always benefit by giving every attempt your best shot.

A unique and surprisingly deep roguelite. There's not really anything quite like it. The artstyle and aesthetic is really cool. The story is about as good as you an expect from a game like this.

Your hero makes his way around the path on his own, autobattling enemies as he encounters them. You play cards from your deck to develop the landscape which allows you to build stats, encounter new types of enemies and/or collect gear & resources. You can equip increasingly better gear onto your hero. Eventually, you fight a boss and then you can return to your base camp with resources. Die and you lose most of what you collected.

At camp, you can unlock cards for your deck (there's a light deckbuilding element), new classes and buffs for future runs.

at times frustrating due to the combination of rng + trying to figure out whats what and whats good, but very satisfying once you figured out a proper setup your character
probably the best game I played to just alt tab and do 2nd monitor stuff while gaming

Love, love this game. I wish they would make a sequel. I have 100% on xbox, the game is not "broken" or unplayable. Far from it! It's very, very grindy, not super clear on objectives, and difficult at times. I love the grind though, the story was interesting, the system itself is super cool. It felt really rewarding to finally beat it 100%. 

If you like to take your time and enjoy an interesting game, Devolver delivers again. <3

LOOP HERO is a lovely retro autobattler-management RPG, where your character walks around on a randomly generated circular path and autobattles enemies spawning in. While this doesn't sound exciting - well, if you die, it's game over so it should be - the card system should. You see, this is a ROUGELITE with a CARD SYSTEM. Every enemy killed or location visited grants you one or multiple of the following randomly:

A) A location card.
B) Equipment to become stronger in battle.
C) A resource.

Location cards are used to enrich the world: place forests, meadows, even farms and graveyards where people may appear. From these locations the hero gets some sort of bonus (or rarely malus) for the current run, but more importantly it may create interactions such as spawning in new enemies, becoming a healing spot, and so on. The interesting part is that LOCATIONS COMBINE, meaning for example a fa

this game is awesome. I have bought it on each system i have had and moved through. Good game "loop" deeper than it looks, li9ke running solo dungeons, quickly, and gathering supplies/loot to build up your town and your strength 3 different classes, four acts, different bosses, cool art design, and little features when you build the path your hero travels that keep things interesting. Don't sleep on this one. I've gotten hours and hours out of it, enjoying each bit.

I love this game. It is very basic and you don't control much, but i find it's good for passing the time when i can't be bothered to play anything else. There's a lot of negative reviews regarding the fact that you don't control much, and it is true. It's like a semi-idle rpg, but if you go into it thinking of it more like a tower defence game you will likely enjoy it. I just play it as an in-between games kinda thing. It's great for what I paid for it (£2), can't go wrong there. Although it might not be for everyone.

😵‍💫 Loop Hero is a unique and well crafted roguelike full of addictive gameplay and progression.

The gameplay "loop" is basically going out on an expedition with 3 heroes to chose from, running around in a looping road. Then the player has his deck/cards to place them anywhere on the tiles around the map, that will spawn more enemies, buffs, debuffs and materials with a dayli timer. You can also find hidden combos with the cards, 2 cards placed next to each other can transform into a new card with its changes or upgrades. Pretty cool system!
And with the auto battler combat, the player has a cool rpg system of leveling up, finding gear with stats and trying to survive and beat the boss spawning later on.

Then after each death, retreat or success of each expedition, the player goes back to his camp and has a whole village to build and progress through with all the collected materials ga
Super unique concept mixing autobattlers, deck building, and tower defense. I really dig the aesthetic and lore too.

If I had to describe Loop Hero to a friend, I'd tell them it is the only game I enjoy there being an auto battle system in. I usually hate those games because it feels like you're not doing anything to effect the outcome of any fight. This game however, has me constantly attached to it with my attention when I play. Micro managing your gear in a run, planning what you are bringing in around what class you pick, and for once I really like the rougeLITE mechanics the game has to offer. I usually play Roguelikes because I see more replayability without permanent upgrades but this game has so much to discover that I find that the ability to play it again and again is much more than others like it. Not to mention the music to boot is amazing if you like the old style of pixelated video game music. I even bought this here on steam after playing it for a while on xbox gamepass and beating the g
great game to zone out and forget about the brain eating parasites

Good little game I picked up for less than $3.
It has a unique take on the "roguelite" formula, combining autobattler/deck building and world building in a way that feels simple but also strategic. 
You don't directly control the character, but you create the path he traverses, placing traps and monsters in his way, which offer a nice balance of risk and reward.
the fun comes from finding which synergies work best together and some secret ones that the game doesn't outright explain.
It can get a little grindy later on and once you've figured out which set up works best for you it becomes pretty easy.
But because of the "one more run" pull and unique and fun gameplay "loop". I feel like Loop Hero is definitely a game that can scratch that "roguelite" itch.

It can be good on sale, but it's very grindy and lack strategic depth, so it's pretty repetitive. 
UI is quite clunky too.

I am going to start by stating that I actually really like this game. What I have do is air a grievance though. This game hasn't been updated in over 3 years at this point, and it has things that were never implemented but were clearly meant to slot in. Either take out the parts that are never going to get added in (Belt and Gloves I believe) or finally put them in. I would also gladly pay for a full content DLC at this point with how cheap the base game is. There just isn't enough in the game as is.

Not my cup of tea, but it's well made and has a lot of heart. It was like catnip to my wife. 

Regardless, good mechanics, good design. and a good recommendation.

I really like the art style, the concept of bringing the world back, seeing how tiles interact with each other and so on. If you like this kind of game, I would recommend "He is Coming" which for me is simply a better executed version of this game. I love the concept of the game, but eventually it's just "I need to grind a bunch of loops in order to unlock things for the boss". There's just not enough depth to it.

Great atmosphere through the art and music, the story is not great but serviceable. Unfortunately the gameplay aspect feels kind of brain dead, as in you can tune out through most of it and do fine. Two weeks from now I probably forget what I even did here.

You could say you want to progress, just for the progression and to see the story end, but the mechanics don't really develop with it. You need to constantly micromanage your character's equipment so you can't really even look away, but I never felt like I had a whole lot of control over how things turned out anyway. I really want to like this game, and trust me I tried. I sunk 10 hours into this, read countless guides, and yet I still can't find any fun in this.

For positives, the music, sound design as a whole is catchy and immersive. the art style and mechanics are incredibly unique and high quality. The story seems intriguing... Now onto the negatives.

The progression is EXTREMELY slow, even using optimal farming methods. This makes the game feel amazingly unrewarding even if you decide to grind it out. 

The game is punishing for deaths, but I'm not marking that against it, I think it's a good thing. It's just a shame that the grindy nature of this game just makes every death feel awful, not because you lost items, but because youre going to have to do multiple runs to build it back up.

The deck building and combinations are obscure, I'm sure this is by design, but for someone like me who lov

One loop you're killing everything easily, next loop you die easily on 1 tile. So how do you decide when to retreat if that's the case almost every time? Do you have to retreat when you're winning easily because the next loop might be one of those where you just die because the game wills it?

The gameplay "loop" is infuriating as hell.

You build the world around you as you loop through a track. Every loop enemies get stronger and you get better gear as well. 

It all fine and dandy when you get a general idea of things. Dont spam enemy spawners like crazy, dont stack them, give breathing room, Unless rng ♥♥♥♥♥ on you try to get a build going, etc.


It dumb as hell though because the jump from one loop to the next is so exponential that one loop youre basically untouchable and have full health by the end of loop to, being killed not even halfway through the next. Its SO infuriating.  The problem is this is a resource/building game and you cant progress without resources. 

You lose 70% on death, or mid loop retreat. The resources aren't just get one of this or that. Its gather 10+ of this tiny resource to make !1! normal resource. Its idiotic. 

Even if you have 1 of the nor

I feel as though a dev would crack a cocky smirk at me if I were to say the game lacks a sense of progression or moving forward and keeps you permanently stuck in a circle, but if I genuinely could not find the "why" of going through this game's repetition in 11 hours, I fear that 100 hours later I'd find the why, and be sorely dissapointed.

TL;DR grindy, repetitive, no sense of real progression.

reviews.title: A New All Time Classic!
reviews.text:
For a game that can be played with just one touch, there is nothing more perfect than this for mobile whilst offering such deep and interesting an experience. I passed up this game for a while, for unknown reasons having the wrong impression of it (perhaps partially from the generic name). This is ultimately a strategy game, even really, a board game.

What defines this game is that, whilst the hero travels around the board, you must strategically choose what challenges to place in their path, balancing risk and reward to help the hero grow stronger. These challenges are drawn with some degree of randomness that you will influence by your placements. All of the things you can place on the board have (usually hidden) reactions and combinations with each other. I have beaten the game once so far and have not found all the interactions yet. [I see those hints in the credits ;) ] All of this

Why didn’t they slow your progress down and force you to buy gems to speed up building progress and play ads every time you loop around the map. I need roadblocks in my game so I lose interest in them after I am forced to drop 10 .99 every day to speed up my building progress. I don’t think the developers understand how gaming works today. You make a game then you strip out all the features and put them behind multiple paywalls and let the player spend small amounts of money until it accumulates to hundreds of dollars then you stop plaiting the game for a week and your so far behind you have to spend more money to catch back up. Instead these geniuses are asking for just one purchase at the INSANE price of $7. You saw that correctly fokes. A game with 20-40 hours of content for 10% of the  price of a AAA game with

reviews.title: Just great! Ton of content for one low price!
reviews.text: I just wanna say how shocked I am by how much is packed into this tiny download. You can quickly tell this title was created by people who love what they are doing. Next I want to say how thankful I am for growing up when I did.. these people posting 1 star reviews due to having to simply pay for a product should honestly be ashamed. Where does that kind of entitlement come from? Their parents? How hard is it to understand that people have worked hard to bring this game to us. Spent time away from their families and loved ones. Stayed up late into the night, giving us the fruit of their blood sweat and tears. Why wouldn’t it be fair to ask for compensation for a provided service? For those of you STILL complaining that this title costs money you should really just be ashamed it this point. It’s a great game. It deserves our praise and our money. Devs thank you all for your hard work!

reviews.title: Great little gem of a game
reviews.text: This game is very addicting, invoking the ‘just one more turn’ mentality. It’s the perfect game for mobile since you can spend minutes on it, or hours if you want. There’s no mobile dark patterns design in here, just a game for the sake of having fun playing. You get a free trial which is the perfect amount of trial to get to know the game, then a small one-time fee to unlock the full game which is still cheaper than the cheapest freemium tier currency purchase on almost every other mobile game these days. The only critique I have is that some of the stats are a bit underpowered. Vampirism drops off in usefulness very fast, and some talents are giving you like +3 hp in turn 5 when enemies are starting to hit for like 20.

reviews.title: Excellent game!
reviews.text: I love this game so much. Third time I've bought it now, and I'm happy to play it some more. I wish I could transfer my save from PC over, but oh well. The only issue I have is that iCloud/Game Center save syncing doesn't work at all. I've tried so many things. Rebooting each device, making sure there isn't a conflicting save on the other device, multiple connection points, giving it several hours to ensure it syncs, copying the save to another slot and seeing if that kicks it in, deleting a fresh save on the other device in hopes of maybe "clearing" space for the save. So far, nothing at all has worked.

reviews.title: A wonderful game
reviews.text: Overall it’s an absolutely amazing game that you should definitely play. The only reason I give it 4 instead of 5 stars: the rng can sometimes really really really screw your run, which is completely understandable in these types of games. But when that happens several runs in a row I pretty much just totally lose interest. It would be AWESOME if the rng could be tweaked so that certain cards would have a higher or lower percent of showing depending on other cards. Like for instance I HATE the village and wheat fields like a passion because my hand will fill up completely full of wheat fields. But I’ll never get a single village card. So the wheat fields are totally unplayable and therefore deleting cards that I WANT to keep. Beyond frustrating. So when that just keeps happening: I’m done.

reviews.title: Perfect iPad Game
reviews.text: I’ve played this game on the computer and loved it, but it’s even better on a mobile device. The gameplay is simple but addictive, with a semi-random nature reminiscent of roguelikes, but with enough consistent progress that you always feel like you succeeded in something, even if you die. It also has a charming setting and story, and it’s as well suited to a 15 minute game as it is to a multi-hour binge. The only thing I wish it had was an expansion, DLC, or sequel - but there’s plenty of content and replayability here! Easy 5/5

reviews.title: There’s nothing like it
reviews.text: Loop Hero is inventing a genre, the way Slay The Spire created roguelite deck builders. Perhaps not the first, but first to get it right. It doesn’t seem like much at first, but give it some time. As you build out your base and learn how to strategically place your map tiles, the game comes alive. The description says you don’t control combat—but by your gear selections and how you arrange the path, you absolutely do. 5 Stars for gameplay, 4 for graphics which I hope are better on a sequel, but turn on the pixel shader, it helps a lot. This is a unique, well designed game I will be playing for a long time.

reviews.title: A real game for your phone!
reviews.text:
It’s so rare these days to get games you can just buy and not get pestered by ads or micro transactions. The free version is just a demo but you buy the full game and it’s the full game no more gotchas. 

The gameplay itself is solid, look it up as the game was a proper PC game before it was ported for the phone. My only gripe is placing tiles sometimes I just want to click on the card to remind myself of its full stats and end up accidentally placing it in a terrible spot but after awhile that’s a rare occurrence.

reviews.title: Great game, one time price!
reviews.text: Found this game originally on the computer. I was ecstatic to see it on the tablet. Very much a hidden gem. This is the first of this game type I have played and I have fallen in love with this gameplay. Pick a class, start a loop, build your challenge, and continue till you can’t. Then bring back the loot and upgrade your camp to unlock story and more classes. I personally use the game wiki to know which cards change others (I know, I am a cheat). Join the fun!

reviews.title: Turning up the speed makes this game awesome
reviews.text:
A unique twist on tower defense, deck building, auto battling, and rogue likes, all in one fun and addictive package.
The trial version gives you plenty of content to decide if this game is for you.
The default settings might feel a bit slow at first, but you have the option to speed up the combat and walking elements, which improves the gameplay a ton and makes it a lot snappier and exciting.

reviews.title: Great game!
reviews.text: I’ve had this on PC for a while and was hoping for a mobile port, finally my dreams come true 😭 I’m not sure why people are leaving negative feedback based on a very clear description, most PC ports cost money on mobile. This game is well worth the price, I’ve gotten a lot of hours out of it on PC. I love the QOL additions like the arrows pointing exactly where your card is under your finger so you know where it will be placed, great port!

reviews.title: Absolutely Outstanding
reviews.text: Didn’t know what to expect going into this but the game definitely did not disappoint. The art style is perfect, very clean with a nice use of colors, the world the game takes place in is interesting and the mechanics of having to rebuild the world piece by piece and the way it was implemented was unique. I’ll probably end up buying it on steam rather than just sticking to my phone.

Vague descriptions on items make for a quite confusing start, forcing you to look it up on google even after you unlock the encyclopedia (which again you’ll need to read the tiny text through. 

Still a very fun game and the devs did a good job getting it to mobile, there’s just some room for QoL improvements.

reviews.title: Addictive but flawed
reviews.text:
The gameplay loop of this game is very addictive and great for mobile but the lack of explanation it gives for resources and how to acquire them is incredibly annoying. You can’t even hover over a resource to see what it’s called, all you have to go on is a blurry sprite. It wasn’t until I watched a tips and tricks video on YouTube that I realized there’s an encyclopedia you unlock associated with one of the last buildings you gain the ability to add to your town. 
Why would the encyclopedia not be available to players from the beginning to they know how to acquire the resources they need to build the next buildings in their town? 
Hoping some updates comes soon that improve the user experience and I can recommend this game to more people.
